stem: Which family history detail is the strongest reason to avoid simple reassurance alone when deciding whether a child's presentation may reflect a broader inherited concern?

options.text: A parent who prefers morning appointments

explanation: Consanguineous parents are the strongest family history clue here because they increase the likelihood of an inherited condition and warrant more careful assessment rather than simple reassurance alone.

citations.source: Louisa Leone MD3 2025 - Child and Adolescent Health - Study Notes.pdf
citations.title: Page 94

optionExplanations.A: Correct because consanguinity increases the chance of autosomal recessive and other inherited conditions, so it is a meaningful red flag in family history.
optionExplanations.B: Incorrect because a family preference for sport has no bearing on inherited disease risk.
optionExplanations.C: Incorrect because appointment preference is unrelated to assessment of inherited or developmental concern.
optionExplanations.D: Incorrect because a grandparent enjoying gardening is not a clinically relevant family history detail.
optionExplanations.E: Incorrect because a sibling liking mathematics is not relevant to the assessment of inherited concern.
